text.p: Discarded England leg-spinner Ian Salisbury snapped up his season's best of six for 19 on Monday to bowl Surrey to their first win of the county championship campaign.
Surrey beat Nottinghamshire by 131 runs after the rival captains had contrived a definite result to the rain-hit match with two declarations on the fourth and last day at The Oval.
Notts declared at their overnight 73 for one, 128 behind on first innings, and Surrey scored 123 for six before their declaration left the visitors needing 252 to win off 59 overs.
Salisbury and Pakistan off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq, who took two for 34 in 26 overs, exploited a wearing pitch to send Notts tumbling from 78 for two to 120 all out.
There was another contrived definite result in a rain-affected match at Worcester where Young England captain Andrew Flintoff spurred Lancashire to their first championship win of the season.
Flintoff hit his career-best of 70 from 101 balls as Lancashire, who needed 236 in 64 overs to beat Worcestershire, recovered from 64 for five to win by three wickets with nearly 12 overs to spare.
Flintoff, who led England's under-19 side in Pakistan in the 1996-97 season, hit 10 fours and a six in only his second championship match.
The all-rounder effectively won the match in a seventh-wicket stand of 98 in 21 overs with wicketkeeper Warren Hegg.
Gloucestershire left-arm fast-medium bowler Mike Smith, named in England's squad for the third Ashes test, took three for 36 in a rain-hit draw against Northamptonshire at Luton.
Smith helped to reduce Northants to 58 for six in reply to Gloucestershire's 180 for six declared in a contest reduced to one innings after rain washed out the first three days.
